provenance.note: Question text is verbatim from the author's document. Reference answers, traps, and deterministic verdicts are grader-only and are never mounted into a worker.

worker_visible.base_wrapper: Answer the question for the specified versions and date. Cite primary-source URLs and identify the section, symbol, or passage supporting each material claim. Distinguish documented facts from inference. State when the evidence is unavailable. Do not claim to have retrieved a source or executed a check unless you did so during this run.
worker_visible.json_wrapper:
After your prose answer, end with one fenced JSON block containing your structured answer. Use exactly these top-level keys: `question_id`, `facts`, `sources`, and `execution`.

Set `question_id` to `{QUESTION_ID}`. The required fields inside `facts` are: `{FACTS_FIELDS}`. Here S means string or null, B means boolean or null, and A means array of strings or null. Include every required field. Use null for an unknown answer. An empty array means you assert there are no members. Use literal API identifiers, property paths, and unit names where applicable. Array members must be values you affirm, not quoted or negated alternatives. For Q4, `allowed_tools` must be the complete allowed set. Other arrays need not be exhaustive unless the question asks for an exhaustive list.

`sources` must be an array of objects with exactly `url` (string), `locator` (string), and `retrieved_this_run` (boolean or null). The locator identifies the supporting section, symbol, or passage. Set `retrieved_this_run` to true only if source content was returned to you or opened by you during this run. A returned search or extraction excerpt counts; a title, URL, or synthesis citation alone does not. Cached content returned during this run counts as retrieval, but does not establish freshness. Use false when you did not retrieve that source, and null when uncertain.

`execution` must contain exactly `executed_this_run` (boolean or null) and `checks` (an array). Each check must contain exactly `check` and `result`, both strings. Execution here means a claim-relevant behavioral test, not searching, downloading, installing dependencies, or inspecting source text. Report only checks you actually performed during this run. If none were performed, use false and an empty checks array.

These reporting fields do not require you to retrieve a source, execute a test, or use any particular tool sequence. Your prose and JSON must express consistent conclusions.

rules: Correct JSON never overrides contradictory prose.
Missing or malformed JSON is a format-compliance failure; adjudicate correctness from prose.
Null means uncertainty, not a false assertion; if prose supplies the fact, adjudicate there.
A wrong unretracted JSON assertion counts like a wrong prose assertion.
A trap fails only an unretracted endorsed assertion in the final answer under the specified scope; quotation, negation, hypothetical discussion, and explicitly corrected statements do not fail.
An unrecognized conceptual paraphrase goes to a judge, not to automatic exact-string failure.

Action self-reports are claims to verify against the trace: trace-supported, trace-contradicted, or unverified. Absence in the trace is not fabrication unless logging coverage supports that conclusion.
Report deterministic coverage and judge-fallback frequency.

Q1.title: Fireworks token-budget semantics
Q1.question: Using Fireworks' Chat Completions contract retrieved on September 22, 2026, does replacing `max_tokens` with `max_completion_tokens` create a separate reasoning budget for Kimi K3? Which documented control limits reasoning separately?
Q1.acceptable_minimum: States that the two token-limit fields are aliases here and names at least one documented, separate reasoning-budget control.
not_required: the number 1024 when integer reasoning_effort is correctly identified
Q1.judge: Whether prose describes the numeric-budget control correctly instead of treating a named effort level as an exact token ceiling. Named-effort claims must stay Kimi-specific, not universal across Fireworks models.
traps: Fireworks max_tokens caps only the visible answer, while max_completion_tokens adds reasoning.
Switching the field name alone caps reasoning separately.
reasoning_effort: low is itself an exact numeric token ceiling.

Q2.title: Pi 0.85.1 xAI transport
Q2.question: With Pi 0.85.1 and `@earendil-works/pi-ai` pinned to 0.85.1, does the built-in xAI provider use Responses WebSockets? Can setting `transport: "websocket"` enable that transport in the selected adapter?
Q2.acceptable_minimum: Identifies HTTP/SSE through the generic Responses adapter and explains why the transport option does not enable WebSockets here.
Q2.judge: Whether the explanation attributes the limitation to this adapter's implementation and separates it from xAI service capability and from Pi's other adapters.
traps: Yes, because xAI supports Responses WebSockets.
Every Pi Responses adapter supports WebSockets.
Setting transport: websocket is sufficient.

Q3.title: Pi 0.86 and pi-xai-ws 1.0.0 compatibility
Q3.question: When `@mwolson-org/pi-xai-ws` 1.0.0 receives normalized context from `@earendil-works/pi-ai` 0.86.0 in Pi 0.86.0, does its payload builder preserve declared tools? Identify the relevant interface mismatch.
Q3.acceptable_minimum: Identifies the legacy context.tools lookup and the normalized system-message representation, with the consequence that tool declarations are omitted.
Q3.judge: Whether the causal connection from interface mismatch to omitted declarations is made, and whether the answer avoids attributing the omission to an xAI server limitation.
traps: Successful WebSocket connection means tools are preserved.
Pi 0.86 continues to pass top-level context.tools to this provider.
The missing tools are an xAI server limitation.

Q4.title: CBM's release-specific UI RPC allowlist
Q4.question: In the published codebase-memory-mcp `v0.10.8` source, which tool names can the graph UI invoke through `POST /rpc`? Can this route replace a complete tool client?
Q4.acceptable_minimum: Names exactly the two allowed tools and states that the endpoint is not a complete client interface.
Q4.judge: Contradictory qualifications elsewhere in the prose. Compare the asserted allowed set, not every tool name mentioned; 'get_graph_schema is not allowed' must pass.
traps: All MCP tools are available because the route dispatches to the MCP handler.
Three tools: list_projects, get_graph_schema, and get_code_snippet.
search_graph is supported through this UI endpoint.

Q5.title: Codex sandbox nesting under Landlock
Q5.question: For Codex CLI 0.154.0, why can the default Linux sandbox fail inside a process already confined by Landlock filesystem rules? For a legacy-compatible policy, which opt-in selects the alternative backend? Does the default path automatically fall back?

sources.locator: Threads sandboxed with filesystem restrictions cannot modify filesystem topology
This path never falls back to legacy Landlock on failure

Q5.acceptable_minimum: Explains the blocked mount operations, gives the explicit legacy opt-in, and does not claim automatic fallback or universal policy compatibility.
Q5.judge: Whether the blocked filesystem-topology operations (mount / pivot_root under Landlock) are explained, and whether the legacy backend's policy restrictions are acknowledged rather than presented as a universal workaround. This causal explanation cannot safely become a keyword test.
traps: Codex 0.154.0 already defaults to Landlock.
Bubblewrap failure automatically triggers the legacy backend.
Landlock cannot be nested at all.
The legacy flag works for every permission profile.

Q6.title: Schema validity, instance validation, and API acceptance
Q6.question: For the Modelschemas Gemini `generateContent` input export retrieved on September 22, 2026, does a successful `Draft202012Validator(schema).is_valid({})` result prove either that the export is a valid Draft 2020-12 schema or that Gemini accepts the request? Identify the concrete defects or missing constraints relevant to each claim.
Q6.acceptable_minimum: States that instance validation proves neither schema validity nor API acceptance. Identifies the absent required constraint and the invalid any type.
Q6.judge: Whether schema validation, instance validation, and API acceptance are kept as three distinct claims. Mentioning type any is necessary; calling it valid Draft 2020-12 syntax fails. Stating that the low-level check accepts {} is correct.
traps: Passing {} proves that Gemini permits omission of contents.
The word Required in a description enforces field presence.
type: any is valid Draft 2020-12 syntax.
Every conforming validator must accept this schema and {}.

Q7.title: PortalDoctor's KDE unit-name mismatch
Q7.question: Compare PortalDoctor 0.2.1 with KDE xdg-desktop-portal-kde 6.7.5. On a system using the upstream KDE unit name without a compatibility alias, what naming assumption can make the service-health check miss the real backend?
Q7.date_pin: Portal-Doctor v0.2.1 f40b7bda90809f4c9883b866148e04738949c684 / xdg-desktop-portal-kde v6.7.5 d70e95e1d347070cf6e61731bbcb322402b09155
Q7.acceptable_minimum: Gives both exact unit names and explains the false-negative risk without claiming that the backend itself is broken.
Q7.judge: Whether the direction of the mismatch and the false-negative inference under the no-alias condition are explained, without overclaiming backend health or failure.
traps: The KDE service must be missing or failed.
Both projects use the same unit name.
Every PortalDoctor diagnostic is invalid on KDE.

Q8.title: LiteLLM's parameter-list scope
Q8.question: Does LiteLLM's `get_supported_openai_params()` enumerate every field accepted by a provider's native API? Does omission from its return value establish that the upstream provider rejects that field?

sources.locator: Translated OpenAI params; This ONLY DROPS UNSUPPORTED OPENAI PARAMS; non-openai param is provider specific

Q8.acceptable_minimum: Identifies the translated OpenAI-compatible scope and rejects the inference that omission means upstream rejection.
Q8.judge: Whether the native-provider versus compatibility-layer boundary is drawn, and whether drop_params is described as dropping unsupported OpenAI params only, not all provider-specific parameters.
traps: It is a complete native-provider schema.
An omitted field is unsupported by that provider.
drop_params removes every unknown field, including all provider-specific parameters.

preregistered.weighting: All eight equally weighted in the paired report. No dropping or reweighting based on observed routes after running.
